> Reproducible in v4.6.dev.custom_build.b79fe2e02 @ Windows 11

Hi @patwork 👋 

Please could you test against my branch in #113048?

It seems to fix the crash for me, but I welcome results from your (Windows) machine, positive or negative!

> Please could you test against my branch in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/113048?

Sorry for the delay. Indeed, after applying your fix, Godot no longer crashes when changing node types. I tried alternating between types Node3D, CharacterBody3D, and RigidBody3D.

From time to time, I receive a message:

```
ERROR: Condition "p_child->data.parent != this" is true.
   at: remove_child (scene/main/node.cpp:1739)
```

but I am not sure if it is related.

That is not a complete fix. The issue is not the node references, but rather the List<>& reference in `SceneTreeDock::_create` pointing directly to `EditorSelection::top_selected_node_list`

See my comment here: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/109515#issuecomment-3601289470

The above may workaround the specific issue for Create Type, but it will not solve the underlying problem. Any function which can invoke a `@tool` script or fire a signal could possibly disrupt the list of nodes in EditorSelection and corrupt the list iterator being used in the for loop.

I think the correct fix is to switch any of the interactive operations that could do something in the middle of the for loop, back to using a List<> copy (or a LocalVector<>).

I don't think it would meaningfully impact performance, given that we are looping through everything in the selection list either way, and it's an interactive operation.

I also don't know how much we expect to support extremely large node selections. Is it common for a user to select 10000-100000 nodes at once? Copying the list of selected nodes is unlikely to be slow in 99.999% of usecases

This is a cache invalidation problem. The cached node was deleted and became a freed pointer. 
~~After applying PR #112401 and #113393, some caches still need to be cleared.~~
- Using `Object::cast_to()` to convert a freed pointer resulted in a crash.
- Memory reuse led to issues similar to #112960.

@Rindbee The List<>& reference will be fixed by this PR:
*  #111837

This issue is not really about cache invalidation, but rather specifically about a regression introduced into SceneTreeDock::_create in 4.6 dev. Object::cast_to isn't the culprit in this specific case, since this issue is a list iterator invalidation issue.

That said if you see anything continuing to happen with change type after applying #111837, file a new issue

Do we know what commit introduced the regression?

CC @KoBeWi @bruvzg

I was able to confirm that removing `&` from here fixes the crash:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/d743736f84fb668bcdfb5bf86258e483f35c6fec/editor/docks/scene_tree_dock.cpp#L3030
This was introduced in #109515

There are more list references used in this file, not sure if they cause problems too.

Also not sure why the selection uses List, it can be changed to Vector/LocalVector. Copying them should be faster, making the reference (hopefully) unnecessary.

Removing the old `Node3D` from the tree triggers a call to `Node3DEditor::update_transform_gizmo()`. When it retrieves the selected nodes via `EditorSelection::get_top_selected_node_list()`, the `EditorSelection::top_selected_node_list` is cleared. 

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/d743736f84fb668bcdfb5bf86258e483f35c6fec/editor/editor_data.cpp#L1226


https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/d743736f84fb668bcdfb5bf86258e483f35c6fec/editor/scene/3d/node_3d_editor_plugin.cpp#L9304

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/d743736f84fb668bcdfb5bf86258e483f35c6fec/editor/scene/3d/node_3d_editor_plugin.cpp#L6830

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/d743736f84fb668bcdfb5bf86258e483f35c6fec/editor/editor_data.cpp#L1357-L1359

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/d743736f84fb668bcdfb5bf86258e483f35c6fec/editor/editor_data.cpp#L1293

Therefore, it doesn't need to be **the scene root**; any `Node3D` object is potentially suitable.
